question.problem:
Which of the following statements are logically equivalent?

I. $¬(A∨B)$

II. $A∨¬B$

III. $¬(A∧B)$
question.worked_solution:
Two statements are logically equivalent if they have the same truth table. So, we construct a truth table for the three given statements:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬(A∨B)\,$ | $\,A∨¬B\,$ | $\,¬(A∧B)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

We see that none of the statements have the same truth table, so none of them are logically equivalent.

Therefore, the correct answer is "None of those listed".
